extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers and diagnostic assay developers (PANDAA-LASV); molecular diagnostics researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Design, optimize, analytically validate, and preliminarily clinically validate a pan-lineage Lassa virus (LASV) probe-based qPCR diagnostic using PANDAA technology; includes in silico design, reagent/buffer optimization, analytical sensitivity/specificity testing, and clinical sample evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prototype performance specifications (Aim 3 milestone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prototype PANDAA-LASV assay with pan-lineage 95% LOD ≤10 RNA copies/reaction, specificity >99% using non-LASV templates, and preliminary clinical sensitivity >95%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim 3 analytical and clinical validation must demonstrate these target metrics; Aim 2 refinement must ensure 95% LOD ≤10 RNA copies/reaction (±2.5 copies) across divergent genomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use WHO Target Product Profile (TPP) as benchmark
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a WHO TPP for Ebola/VHF as a model to set preliminary performance specifications and operational targets for PANDAA-LASV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PANDAA-LASV preliminary specifications (as compared to the Ebola TPP model) include >95% sensitivity, >99% specificity, ~3–5 procedural steps, and ~90 minutes time-to-result. Use the WHO TPP as a guide for acceptable/desirable trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primer-binding site selection criteria (Aim 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify most conserved regions (top 5% by rank, n=6) from genome-wide diversity data; design 25–40 bp forward and reverse non-PANDAA primers within these regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design criteria: (a) forward and reverse primers' 3' termini are proximal to the same strictly conserved base; (b) the 5' terminus of each primer is at a conserved base; annealing temperature (Tm) is rarely a consideration for PANDAA site selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: PANDAA primer design rules (PDR/ADR/LNA/degeneracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: PANDAA primers contain a 3' adaptor region (ADR) matched to the probe-binding site and a pan-degenerate region (PDR) incorporating nucleotide degeneracy; LNA bases placed at 100% conserved positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate high degeneracy (empirically determined, range ~75–95% — i.e., include nucleotides with frequency 5–25%) in the PDR; ADRs must perfectly match probe-binding sequence and are selected during probe evaluation; LNA placement enhances mismatch intolerance and reduces non-specific dimer formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primer degeneracy and specificity tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: High primer degeneracy (example values: forward primer up to ~41,472-fold degenerate; reverse primers combined degeneracy up to ~34,560-fold) is acceptable and does not necessarily yield detrimental non-specific products in PANDAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical in-silico evaluation and experimental verification required; non-specific products should be checked by agarose gel; expect cumulative primer pools of tens to hundreds of thousands of distinct sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primer selection workflow and sensitivity ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate ~6 forward and ~6 reverse primers per conserved region (~36 primer pairs per region on a 96-well plate) and rank primer sets by sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 5' CMV-sequence tag in reverse primers to isolate amplification performance from probe-binding effects; rank primer sets based on lowest Cq at 10^1 copies/reaction and select pair with greatest sensitivity for each region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probe design criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Design LASV-specific probes matching the most common LASV haplotype at the selected primer-binding site; probes usually 11–15 nucleotides in length and with predicted Tm between 56–60°C; evaluate forward and reverse orientations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize probes of various lengths and orientations in silico; select probes with highest sensitivity and shortest effective length; probe-binding site position is dependent on chosen primer-binding sites because PANDAA primers adapt probe-binding sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primer/probe evaluation concentrations and initial buffer
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary evaluations performed with 200 nM primers in the customized PANDAA PRxB real-time PCR buffer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain primer concentration at 200 nM during buffer optimization steps; negative controls and replicate schemes as described elsewhere must be applied during selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicates and negative control scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative controls: 0.05 ng/reaction human genomic DNA only. Replicate scheme: reactions containing >10^4 copies/reaction performed in triplicate; reactions <10^4 copies/reaction performed in 15 replicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative control reactions should be analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis to ensure absence of products. Use consistent replicate rules throughout Aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: qPCR signal calling (positive/negative) and data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: qPCR Cq data will be log-transformed and plotted relative to input copy number. Define positive signal as Cq < 37 cycles and negative as Cq > 37 cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply cutoffs consistently across experiments; use Cq<37 as the positive threshold for analytical sensitivity calculations and performance comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction buffer optimization criteria (Aim 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize amplification through reaction buffer development/refinement (PRxB as starting formulation). MgCl2 will be titrated from 3.5–7.0 mM; primer concentrations held at 200 nM; optimize polymerase and reverse transcriptase concentrations/ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose MgCl2 concentration that yields the lowest limit of detection (LOD) without introducing non-specific signal in negative controls. Evaluate alternative buffers (12 formulations) from an industry collaborator if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay optimization strategies (asymmetrical PCR, ProAmp, 5‑nitroindole)
rubrics_metrics.description: If required, incorporate assay optimizations such as asymmetrical PCR (increase the primer that generates the probe target template), PANDAA ProAmp to offset low early-cycle amplification efficiency, and inclusion of universal base 5‑nitroindole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using universal bases that reduce Tm, offset with LNA placements at 100% conserved nucleotides; apply empirical optimization workflows refined during PANDAA-HIV development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative refinement across divergent genotypes (Aim 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate Aim 1 reagents on a LASV diversity panel; evaluate sensitivity across strains, determine LODs for each strain by 2-fold serial dilutions, and iteratively update primer/probe design to normalize detection across lineages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select reagents with lowest LOD across strains for further optimization. Use design elements from prior PANDAA work (paired degenerate primers/probes, LNA placement, universal bases) to overcome lineage-specific performance differences and ensure 95% LOD ≤10 copies/rxn (±2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical sensitivity validation protocol (Aim 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine 95% LOD of PANDAA-LASV on RNA templates representing nine strains by Probit analysis; run GPC RT‑PCR/2007 in parallel for comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 384-well plates, run 64 reactions per strain across dilutions (10^4–10^1 cp/rxn) plus 64 negative-control reactions per plate; repeat across nine plates (one per strain) to generate Probit-based LOD estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: LASV spiked sera LOD determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine PANDAA-LASV LOD from sera by spiking LASV (Josiah) RNA into normal human serum at 10^4–10^0 copies/mL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess LOD in the presence of serum matrix effects to confirm clinical/analytical sensitivity from biologically relevant sample types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical specificity testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate nucleic acid from related arenaviruses, other viral hemorrhagic fevers (VHFs), and pathogens circulating in West Africa across 10-fold serial dilutions over three orders of magnitude to assess cross-reactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze reactions on agarose gel to identify potential amplification products not detected by qPCR; include purified total RNA from pooled normal human sera diluted across six 10-fold dilutions with 64 PANDAA-LASV reactions per dilution to confirm negative signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis and statistical criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze data using generalized linear models and confidence interval functions in R to quantify median and 95% LOD for each strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect LOD deviation <25% across lineages; quantify median and 95% LOD with confidence intervals. Compare PANDAA-LASV performance to the GPC RT‑PCR/2007 benchmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity troubleshooting and mitigation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: If non-specific signal occurs (including homologous sequences in non-LASV templates), confirm products by sequencing and apply mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigations include: (a) incorporate mismatch-intolerant LNA bases at sites conserved within LASV but divergent in other species; (b) adjust MgCl2 concentrations (small adjustments often change specificity more than sensitivity); (c) fine-tune custom buffer formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls for extraneous template/background
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare LASV viral RNA samples from cultured virus eluted in a background of cellular nucleic acid to test assay sensitivity in the presence of extraneous template; template normalization performed with Aldatu protocols targeting non-LASV sequence at the 3' end of synthetic templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate matrix/background to ensure LOD measurements reflect realistic sample conditions (e.g., presence of cellular nucleic acids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and select-agent handling criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Work will be performed exclusively with inactivated, purified Lassa virus RNA certified by commercial vendors or partners; these non-viable reagents are excluded from select agent regulations and can be handled at BSL-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain vendor certification of inactivation; obtain nucleic acid for other select agents similarly certified; document biosafety status and ensure compliance with exclusion criteria in 42 CFR/9 CFR/7 CFR where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data benchmarks and use of prior PANDAA-HIV experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data showed PANDAA reagents detected divergent LASV strains with near-equal sensitivity and matched or exceeded sensitivity of the GPC RT‑PCR/2007 assay for a reference strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior PANDAA-HIV reagent design, PRxB mastermix performance, and sample-in/answer-out timelines (e.g., ~2 hours for HIV genotypic resistance test) as supporting benchmarks and inform optimization strategies for LASV assay development.
